run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:39:07Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is matched by a real, sharp rise in the error status of spans attributed to service frontend-proxy: the 5-minute error-span rate was 0.0037–0.018/s through the 01:39:07 sample, then 0.5208 at 01:41:07, 1.537 at 01:44:07, 1.689 at 01:47:07 and 1.270 at 01:50:07. The errors sit on frontend's outbound grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds path (and the frontend GET/api/data path that calls it), and the same errors appear on frontend-proxy's ingress and router frontend egress spans. At the same time the ad service's own spans collapsed (GetAds 5m rate 0.6 at 01:41:07, then 0 at 01:44:07, 01:47:07 and 01:50:07), its container in pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 was OOMKilled (exit 137, finishedAt 01:38:36Z), and its stdout stops at 01:38:33.817Z with no later lines through 01:50. Chaos-mesh evidences a Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos that spawned a JVMChaos experiment roughly every minute from 01:38:01 to 01:47:08, each Applied event naming 'otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25/ad' and most Recovered 45–60s later. The ad Deployment, frontend and frontend-proxy pods were not rolled out or restarted (frontend/frontend-proxy restartCount 0; pod templates unchanged, ad pod created 01:01:32 like its siblings), and the flagd ad fault flags read as 'off'. The fault-applying object is therefore the chaos Schedule, but the conclusion is partial: the JVMChaos/Schedule specs (injected action, selector, duration) could not be read with the permitted resource kinds, the RequestErrorRate rule itself was not found in the queried Prometheus, and the alert's stated value 1.5333 does not match the 5m error-span rate at its own anchor 01:39:07.

claims.text: trace span error rate for service_name frontend-proxy (status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR) was 0.0037–0.018 per second through the 01:39:07 sample point, then rose to 0.5208 at 01:41:07, 1.537 at 01:44:07, 1.689 at 01:47:07 and 1.270 at 01:50:07, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET stayed around 19–21/s.

The same error rise appears on service frontend (error-span rate 1.054 at 01:41:07 rising to 3.07/3.36/2.47) and its errors are on the operations GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect; frontend-proxy's errors are on ingress and router frontend egress only, i.e. the request path that carries the frontend's AdService call.

The ad service's own span rate collapsed at the same time: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 5m rate was 0.6 at the 01:41:07 sample and 0 at 01:44:07, 01:47:07 and 01:50:07, and getRandomAds/getAdsByCategory likewise fell to 0, meaning ad stopped producing server spans during the window.

Pod ad-554b849958-fcl25, container ad, has restartCount 1 with lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 2026-11-18T01:01:35Z and finishedAt 2026-11-18T01:38:36Z; the pod is Running and Ready with podIP 100.96.4.112 and remains the single address of the otel-demo service 'ad' (port 8080).

Container logs of ad-554b849958-fcl25 show normal ad request handling lines up to 2026-11-18T01:38:33.817Z; a bounded fetch for 01:38:30Z–01:50:00Z returned only 14 lines, all inside 01:38:30–01:38:33.817, and the unfiltered newest-100-of-2744 read also ended at 01:38:33.817, so no ad application output was returned after the OOMKill/restart.

Events in namespace chaos-mesh show Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos spawning child objects every ~60 seconds: Spawned otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos-4c7dg at 01:38:01, then -tdvvl 01:39:01, -7fjbx 01:40:12, -7zk5w 01:41:08, -t8tf2 01:42:04, -9jglq 01:43:01, -9626f 01:44:14, -t4jlc 01:45:11, -452d7 01:46:09 and -qttkp 01:47:08.

Every one of those spawned JVMChaos objects records an Applied event with the message 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25/ad' (first at 01:38:11 for -4c7dg, last at 01:45:21 for -t4jlc), and most then record TimeUp and 'Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25/ad' about 45–60s later; the last spawn otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos-qttkp at 01:47:08 has no Recovered/TimeUp event in the collected events.

Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos (namespace chaos-mesh) is the object that applied the fault to pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 / container ad inside the incident window: its Spawned events create the JVMChaos experiments whose Applied events name that exact pod and container, and the first experiment (applied 01:38:11) precedes the container's OOMKill at 01:38:36 and the frontend/frontend-proxy error rise from the 01:41:07 sample.

The ad Deployment was not rolled out or reconfigured: replicas 1, readyReplicas 1, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, container limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi, requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi, observedGeneration 1, and its Available condition lastTransitionTime 01:38:37Z coincides with the container restart; the pod was created 2026-11-18T01:01:32Z, the same time as the other demo pods.

The alerting service's own pods were not restarted or recreated: frontend-675fd7b5c5-cmhqq (created 01:01:32Z) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-whhck (created 01:01:34Z) both have restartCount 0 and no last termination reason, and the frontend-proxy pod exposes only the operations 'ingress' (server) and 'router frontend egress' (client).

The error-status series returned for other services show checkout, payment, accounting and fraud-detection at 0 and recommendation at ~0.004 for every sample in the window, i.e. no comparable error burst outside frontend/frontend-proxy was observed in that query's returned series.

Feature-flag driven ad failure is not supported by the readable configuration: in ConfigMap flagd-config the flags adFailure, adHighCpu and adManualGc (descriptions 'Fail ad service', 'Triggers high cpu load in the ad service', 'Triggers full manual garbage collections in the ad service') all have defaultVariant 'off', and the flagd pod flagd-54b69c4c98-mb2t5 has restartCount 0.

A failure originating in frontend or frontend-proxy themselves (crash, restart or rollout) is rejected: both pods have restartCount 0 and were created ~01:01Z, while frontend's error spans are confined to the outbound AdService/GetAds call path and the frontend-proxy spans that mirror it.

The JVM chaos repeatedly applied by Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos to container ad (most plausibly a JVM stress/GC-type injection) is what kept the ad service from serving after 01:38 and pushed its JVM past the 450Mi container limit, producing the OOMKilled exit 137; the exact injected action cannot be confirmed because the JVMChaos and Schedule specs are not readable.

Because ad's pod is Ready and still the only endpoint of service ad while it produced no spans and no logs after 01:38:33Z, requests appear to have been accepted at connection level but not served; this could be a hung/blocked JVM (chaos latency/exception) rather than an empty endpoint set, which is not resolvable from the available metrics.

Read the actual chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos and the JVMChaos children (spec.action, selector, duration) in namespace chaos-mesh, and check whether the Schedule still exists and is still spawning after 01:47:08, to confirm the injected JVM fault and whether it continues.

Check the ad container's memory usage against its 450Mi limit and its JVM heap settings, since the only restart observed was OOMKilled exit 137 during the first chaos experiment; also review whether the readiness probe on the ad pod can pass while the JVM is not serving.

gaps: The chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos and its JVMChaos children could not be read as objects (those kinds are not in the permitted resource list), so the injected JVM action (e.g. stress, latency, exception, GC), its selector, duration and whether it is still active remain unknown.
The RequestErrorRate alerting rule was not found in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data), so its expression, metric and threshold are unverified.

The alert annotation's current value 1.5333 at anchor 2026-11-18T01:39:07Z does not match the 5m frontend-proxy error-span rate at that instant (0.0037), while 1.537 appears at the 01:42:07 sample; the clock/aggregation relationship between the alert and the metric data is unexplained and no conclusion about a latency or count trend at the anchor is drawn.

Jaeger returned no traces after about 2026-11-18T01:14:13Z (ad trace search window ended there; searches for frontend/frontend-proxy in 01:30–01:50Z returned nothing), so error messages, span-level gRPC/HTTP status and per-request durations for the failing calls are unavailable.

Metric series that could show HTTP/gRPC status codes of the failing calls were not present: get_series for http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned nothing and rate(rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{service_name="frontend"}) returned nothing, so 5xx vs timeout vs connection-refused cannot be distinguished from metrics.

Services cart, currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote and shipping returned no error-status series in the by-service error query; their error state is unknown rather than zero, so their impact was not assessed.
The change-history integration is not available, so who created or modified the chaos Schedule and when (and when the flagd flag values were last set) cannot be verified.

Whether any ad requests reached the container between 01:38:36Z and 01:50Z and hung, versus never arriving, is unknown: ad produced no spans and no logs, and no ad-side rpc server count series was available to separate the two.
next_steps: Inspect the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos and the spawned JVMChaos resources (spec.action, selector, duration, desiredPhase) to identify the exact injected JVM fault and whether it is still scheduled.

Compare ad container memory working set and JVM heap usage with the 450Mi limit around 01:38Z, and review the ad readiness probe type, to judge how a JVM fault turned into an OOMKill and an apparently serving-but-blocked endpoint.

Review Alertmanager/Prometheus rule definitions for RequestErrorRate outside the queried Prometheus instance to reconcile the reported value 1.5333 with the span-derived error rate and to confirm which metric the alert uses.
